description:
## Problem

Reach detects :erlang.binary_to_term (unsafe deserialization) and String.to_atom (atom table exhaustion) as security issues. Catseye should detect these too.

## Evidence

From reach:
- reach/lib/reach/smell/checks/unsafe_binary_to_term.ex: detects :erlang.binary_to_term without [:safe]
- reach/lib/reach/smell/checks/unsafe_atom.ex: detects String.to_atom/1 on dynamic input

From facet_pi:
- reach/plugins/quickbeam/javascript_frontend.ex uses String.to_atom extensively

## Expected Behavior

- :erlang.binary_to_term should be flagged as InsecureDeserialization (BEAM term deserialization can lead to RCE)
- String.to_atom should be flagged as a resource exhaustion risk (atom table is limited)

## Suggested Fix

1. Add to rules/elixir-sinks.kdl or create new Elixir-UnsafeDeserialization rule:
   - sink ":erlang.binary_to_term" arg=0 { sanitizer ":safe" }

2. Add to rules/elixir-sinks.kdl or create new Elixir-AtomExhaustion rule:
   - sink "String.to_atom" arg=0 { sanitizer "String.to_existing_atom" }
   - sink "Module.concat" arg=0 { sanitizer "Module.safe_concat?" }
title: Elixir: add :erlang.binary_to_term and String.to_atom as security sinks
